verifyNotes: Confirm against the official exam page (databricks.com/learn/certification/genai-engineer-associate) and the current exam guide PDF (https://www.databricks.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/databricks-certified-gen-ai-associate-exam-guide-august-2026.pdf; exam published 18 Mar 2026): 45 scored multiple-choice/multiple-selection items plus up to 10 unscored, 90 minutes, USD 200, online proctored (the web page also mentions test centres; report which), English/Japanese/pt-BR/Korean, valid 2 years, no published passing score. Weights: Design Applications 14, Data Preparation 14, Application Development 30, Assembling and Deploying 22, Governance 8, Evaluation and Monitoring 12. Use current names from docs.databricks.com: Agent Bricks (Knowledge Assistant, Multi-Agent Supervisor, Information Extraction), Mosaic AI Agent Framework, MLflow 3 (tracing, GenAI evaluation, scorers, LLM judges, Prompt Registry), Mosaic AI Vector Search, Model Serving, Foundation Model APIs, AI Gateway, inference tables, ai_query(), Unity Catalog, Databricks Apps, Genie, managed MCP servers. If something was renamed, teach the current name and mention the exam guide's name. Never copy the guide's sample questions.
name: Databricks Certified Generative AI Engineer Associate
audience: Engineers building RAG apps and agents on Databricks, with about six months of hands-on experience
format: 45 scored multiple-choice and multiple-selection items (up to 10 more unscored) in 90 minutes; online proctored; English, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese, Korean. Databricks publishes no passing score; this site uses 700 on a 100–1000 scale for its mocks.
scenarios: Multi-agent supervisor for sales analytics with Genie
Contract field extraction at scale with ai_query()
Regulated healthcare chatbot with PII masking

domains.name: Design Applications
skills: Prompts for formatted output; selecting model tasks and chain components; translating business goals into pipeline inputs and outputs
Defining and ordering tools for multi-stage reasoning; when to use Agent Bricks (Knowledge Assistant, Multi-Agent Supervisor, Information Extraction)

domains.name: Data Preparation
skills: Chunking strategies (incl. advanced) for document structure and model limits; filtering extraneous content; Python packages for document extraction
Writing chunks to Delta tables in Unity Catalog; choosing source documents; retrieval metrics and evaluation; re-ranking

domains.name: Application Development
skills: LangChain and similar tools; prompt augmentation and prompt adjustment; guardrails; qualitative assessment of quality and safety
Selecting LLMs, embedding models and context length; model hubs and model cards; choosing models from experiment metrics
MLflow and Agent Framework for agentic systems; evaluation vs monitoring in the lifecycle; multi-agent systems with Genie spaces or the conversational API

domains.name: Assembling and Deploying Applications
skills: pyfunc chains with pre/post-processing; RAG building blocks (flavor, embedding model, retriever, dependencies, input example, signature); registering to Unity Catalog with MLflow

Mosaic AI Vector Search: concepts, creating and querying indexes, configuring for scale, freshness, latency and cost; Foundation Model APIs; access control for serving endpoints; ai_query() batch inference

Persistent memory stores; CI/CD (index updates, prompt promotion, component tests); managed, external and custom MCP servers; Prompt Registry versioning; user interfaces (Databricks Apps, Slack, Teams)

domains.name: Governance
skills: Masking as a guardrail; guardrails against malicious inputs; legal and licensing requirements of data sources; mitigating problematic text in source data

domains.name: Evaluation and Monitoring
skills: Choosing LLM size/architecture from metrics; key monitoring metrics; MLflow evaluation, scorers, LLM judges (which need ground truth), tracing; SME feedback
Inference tables, Agent Monitoring, AI Gateway (usage tables, rate limits); controlling LLM costs
